title: Trump Used Newsom's Dyslexia as an Insult and a Disqualifier
description_short: Trump Used Newsom's Dyslexia as an Insult and a Disqualifier
description_medium: Trump said Gavin Newsom should never be allowed to be president because he had admitted to dyslexia, pairing the claim with his usual dumb-guy taunts. This belongs in the archive not because it is the worst thing he has ever done but because it is such a clean moral sample. The reflex is mockery, the target is disability, and the point is public humiliation.
description_long: Trump said California Governor Gavin Newsom should not be president because Newsom had disclosed that he has dyslexia, and paired the argument with insults about his intelligence. The comments made a learning disability part of a political attack on a possible opponent. Dyslexia is a learning difference; its presence does not by itself determine a person’s intelligence, qualifications, or ability to govern. Newsom’s disclosure did not make him ineligible for office, and Trump’s remarks did not change any legal qualification. Their significance lies in using a disability as a reason to discredit a political figure and in directing public mockery at a trait shared by many people. The remarks used a disclosed disability to discredit a political rival and invite public mockery of a trait shared by many people. The remarks shifted attention from Newsom’s record to the fact that he had disclosed a disability.
